arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Srebnick argued the Sixth Amendment protects the right to spend one's own money on counsel.
Mr. Dreeben argued the principle from Monsanto resolves the case regarding substitute property.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned how defendants manage daily expenses under a total freeze.
Justice Kennedy asked about the difficulty of tracing assets to determine their taint.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Luis argues the Sixth Amendment protects her right to spend her own clean money on legal counsel. The government contends the freeze order is valid because it targets proceeds from drug activity. The lower court upheld the freeze, and Luis seeks reversal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between government power and individual rights. It determines whether defendants can access their own funds for legal defense. The outcome shapes pretrial procedures for all criminal defendants.
